question: A 58-year-old man reported a history of 3 weeks of evolution with progressive, moderately painful skin lesions on his left arm. It had started as an erythematous lesion on his left thumb. It had reddish streaks visible as connecting lines between the lesions. The patient did not present fever or other general symptoms. He had been working in his garden but could not remember having any injuries. The etiological diagnosis was made by culture of a skin biopsy. What is the most likely causative agent of this process?

paths: (Left upper arm structure)-PART_OF->(Sensorimotor Cortex)-PART_OF->(Hand)-PART_OF->(Limb structure)-PART_OF->(Left thumb)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Skin lesions on left arm -> started as erythematous lesion on left thumb -> reddish streaks visible as connecting lines between lesions -> no fever or general symptoms -> working in garden without injuries -> culture of skin biopsy for etiological diagnosis -> most likely causative agent is Sporotrichosis -> 95%

enhanced_information: The most likely causative agent of the skin lesions on the left arm, starting from the left thumb with reddish streaks, without fever or general symptoms, and associated with working in the garden, is Sporotrichosis. This is supported by the culture of a skin biopsy. Evidence paths confirm the predisposition of the skin lesion to inflammation and the association of the biopsy procedure with Sporotrichosis.
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 58-year-old man with progressive, moderately painful skin lesions on his left arm, starting from the left thumb with reddish streaks, and a history of working in the garden, aligns with the classic presentation of Sporotrichosis. The absence of fever or general symptoms is also typical of this fungal infection. The confirmation of the diagnosis through a skin biopsy culture further supports this conclusion.
